issue: Whether federal courts of appeals may review colorable constitutional claims notwithstanding the Adam Walsh Act and 8 U.S.C. § 1252(a)(2)(B)(ii)

sides.position: Constitutional claims are not reviewable outside a petition for review of a final removal order, so the court lacks jurisdiction over them
Courts may review colorable constitutional claims (those with some possible validity) despite § 1252(a)(2)(B)(ii)
Constitutional claims are addressed on the merits without specifying a jurisdictional threshold
Assumes, without deciding, that colorable constitutional claims are reviewable

quote: Our sister circuits have split over whether constitutional claims are reviewable notwithstanding the Adam Walsh Act and section 1252(a)(2)(B)(ii).
cite: Anqi Liu v. Markwayne Mullin, No. 25-1652 (7th Cir. 2026)
